subject: CLAS
title: First Year Seminar: Classical Studies
description: Seminar on a theme relevant to Classical Studies. Approaches and sources for consideration are drawn from literature, history, or archaeology of the ancient Mediterranean, depending on the instructor and topic.

restrictions.text: Open only to newly admitted U0 or U1 students.

notes: Maximum 25 students. Students may take only one first year seminar (FYS). Students who register for more than one FYS will be obliged to withdraw from all but one seminar.

subject: CLAS
title: Greece and Rome
description: Introduction to ancient Greek and Roman civilization, focusing on key themes, problems, and methods of the discipline of classical studies.

subject: CLAS
title: Greek Mythology
description: A survey of the myths and legends of Ancient Greece.

subject: CLAS
title: Introductory Latin 1
description: A course designed for beginners with little or no background in Latin. Introduction to basic grammar, vocabulary, morphology. Reading of simple sentences and connected passages.

prerequisites.text: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 210D1/D2 prior to September 2016.

restrictions.text: Pre-requisite(s): Not open to students who have taken CLAS 210D1/D2 prior to September 2016.

subject: CLAS
title: Introductory Latin 2
description: Continued introduction to Latin grammar, vocabulary, and morphology. Reading of more complex sentences and longer connected passages.

prerequisites.text: CLAS 210 or equivalent.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 210D1/D2 prior to September 2016.

notes: Winter

subject: CLAS
title: Intensive Introductory Latin
description: A course designed for beginners with little or no background in Latin. Intensive introduction to grammar, vocabulary, morphology; the reading of sentences and connected passages. Equivalent to CLAS 210 and 212.

subject: CLAS
title: Introductory Ancient Greek 1
description: A course designed for beginners with little or no background in ancient Greek. Introduction to basic grammar, vocabulary, morphology. Reading of simple sentences and connected passages.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 220 D1/D2 prior to September 2016.

subject: CLAS
title: Introductory Ancient Greek 2
description: Continued introduction to ancient Greek grammar, vocabulary, and morphology. Reading of more complex sentences and longer connected passages.

restrictions.text: Not open to student who have taken CLAS 220D1/D2.

notes: Pre-quisite(s): CLAS 220 or equivalent

subject: CLAS
title: Intensive Introductory Ancient Greek
description: A course designed for beginners with little or no background in ancient Greek. Intensive introduction to grammar, vocabulary, morphology; the reading of sentences and connected passages. Equivalent to CLAS 220 and 222.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 220 or CLAS 222.

subject: CLAS
title: Introductory Modern Greek
description: A course for beginners.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 236, CLAS 237 or CLAS 238.

notes: Students must register for both CLAS 230D1 and CLAS 230D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both CLAS 230D1 and CLAS 230D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: CLAS
title: Introduction to Classical Archaeology
description: Introduction to the archaeology of the ancient Greek and Roman Mediterranean through a survey of major sites, artifacts and monuments. Emphasis on archaeological theory and methodology.

subject: CLAS
title: Ancient Greek Literature and Society
description: Survey of ancient Greek literature in translation, covering the key genres and texts in their social and historical contexts. The material to be discussed includes Archaic epic, lyric, and elegy; Classical tragedy, comedy, and historiography; Hellenistic poetry, and literature of the Roman Imperial period.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 200.

subject: CLAS
title: Roman Literature and Society
description: An exploration of Roman texts written during the Republican and Imperial periods (200 BCE-400 CE) and the study of social contexts in which they were written.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 208.

subject: CLAS
title: Ancient Greek Religion
description: Focus on the history of Greek religion in the Classical Period. Particular attention will be paid to the Greek concept of divinity, local pantheons, civic festival calendars, the topography of myth and ritual, ideas concerning the afterlife, mystery cults, oracles and games and the literary representations of religion.

prerequisites.text: CLAS 203 or HIST 205 or permission of instructor.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 380.

subject: CLAS
title: Ancient Greek Democracy
description: Examines the conceptual history of popular government in the context of Greek political culture, from the 6th century BCE to the Roman conquest of Greece.

prerequisites.text: HIST 205 or HIST 231 or permission of instructor.

subject: CLAS
title: Roman Religion
description: Approaches to and problems of Roman religion. The formation of religious topography, problems of religion and empire, the religious interaction between Rome and other Mediterranean peoples, the complex discourse between religion and philosophy, the reformulation of Roman religion during the imperial period, and the rise of Christianity within a pagan Roman world.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 381.

subject: CLAS
title: Classics in Modern Media
description: Receptions of the classical paradigm of Ancient Greece and Rome in modern media, the classical tradition, and current scholarship.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 206.

subject: CLAS
title: Gender in the Ancient World
description: An exploration of gender roles in the Ancient Mediterranean world.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 370.

subject: CLAS
title: Intermediate Latin 1
description: Review of Latin grammar, morphology, syntax, and vocabulary while introducing students to techniques and strategies for reading Latin poetry and prose.

prerequisites.text: CLAS 210 or CLAS 212 or permission of instructor.

subject: CLAS
title: Intermediate Latin 2
description: Continued mastery of the language, with emphasis on translation of Latin texts.

prerequisites.text: CLAS 310 or permission of the instructor.

subject: CLAS
title: Intermediate Latin 2: Selections
description: A study of selected works in Latin. Topic varies by year.

prerequisites.text: CLAS 310 or permission of the instructor

subject: CLAS
title: Intermediate Ancient Greek 1
description: Review of grammar, vocabulary, and syntax of Ancient Greek through translation of selected ancient texts.

prerequisites.text: CLAS 220 or permission of instructor

subject: CLAS
title: Intermediate Ancient Greek 2
description: Continued mastery of the language, with emphasis on translation of ancient Greek texts.

prerequisites.text: CLAS 320 or permission of the instructor

subject: CLAS
title: Intermediate Ancient Greek 2: Selections
description: Translation of ancient Greek texts selected from a given topic, theme, genre, or author. Texts and authors change from year to year.

prerequisites.text: CLAS 320 or permission of instructor.

subject: CLAS
title: Intermediate Modern Greek 1
description: Oral and written competence in the language at the intermediate level through the study of grammar and vocabulary. Excerpts from literature, film and music introducing the civilization of modern Greece.

prerequisites.text: CLAS 230 or similar course or permission of the instructor

subject: CLAS
title: Intermediate Modern Greek 2
description: A thorough review of the language at the intermediate level through the study of grammar, vocabulary and derivatives. Excerpts in prose, poetry and newspapers as well as audiovisual material introducing the civilization of modern Greece. a continuation of CLAS 331.

prerequisites.text: CLAS 331 or similar course or permission of instructor.

subject: CLAS
title: Modern Greek Culture and Society
description: Offers a panorama of Greek culture and society through the study of a corpus of documents in Greek pertaining to the year's thematic topic.
notes: The language of instruction is English. Knowledge of Greek is not mandatory.

subject: CLAS
title: Modern Greek Literature
description: Offers a panorama of Modern Greek literature in translation. It examines a corpus of texts selected according to each year's thematic topic of study.

prerequisites.text: CLAS 220 or CLAS 335 or HIST 349 or permission of instructor

subject: CLAS
title: Life in the Ancient Greek and Roman City
description: The impact of cities and urban living in the development of Greek and Roman society. The work of modern urban theorists frames investigation of the urban form and experience, with an emphasis on archaeology.

prerequisites.text: CLAS 201, CLAS 240, HIST 205, or permission of the instructor.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 348 when topic was "Life in the Ancient Greek and Roman City".

subject: CLAS
title: People and Environment in the Ancient World
description: The environmental history of the ancient Mediterranean through archaeological and art historical remains. The humanistic and material approaches to what the ancients built, modified, destroyed, and renewed as they engaged with and manipulated the “natural” world and resources around them. The details of what the Mediterranean environment was, and how the Greeks and Romans viewed their environmental contexts, while also shaping them to their needs and wants. Investigation of the Mediterranean’s environmental diversity and consideration of how the ancient context might be informative for our contemporary challenges with climate change.

prerequisites.text: CLAS 201, CLAS 240, HIST 205, or permission of the instructor.

subject: CLAS
title: Topics: Classical Archaeology
description: Study of a theme, subject, or question, concentrating on selected physical sites, monuments, artifacts, or other case studies in classical archaeology.

prerequisites.text: HIST 205 or CLAS 240 or permission of instructor

notes: This course may occasionally be taught during the summer term at a site or sites in the Mediterranean as a field studies course.

subject: CLAS
title: Archaeology Fieldwork: Italy
description: Field course offering an introduction to archaeological field methods and laboratory work, and discussion of theoretical interpretation of archaeological data in the context of an Italian archaeological site potentially across multiple time periods (prehistoric, pre-Roman, Roman, late antique and medieval). Taught in Italy.

prerequisites.text: Permission of instructor

notes: Taught in Italy during the summer. Course typically includes visits to cultural, historical or archaeological sites. Students are responsible for their own airfare to Italy.

There is a fee of $3013.46 for the McGill Salapia Field School in Italy associated with registration in CLAS 349. The fee includes shared apartment accommodation for groups of four students, meals (breakfast, lunch and dinner M-R and breakfast and lunch M-F), field tools and weekday transportation to and from the dig site. Students are responsible for their own travel arrangements to Puglia and travel insurance costs.

subject: CLAS
title: Special Topics in Classics
description: A study of a topic in ancient Greek or Roman literature and culture. Ancient texts taught in translation; students require no knowledge of ancient Greek or Latin. Topics varies by year.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 347.

subject: CLAS
title: Ancient Drama and Theatre
description: A synchronic study of ancient Drama from Greece to Rome with a focus on historical and performance context in addition to literary interpretation.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 300.

subject: CLAS
title: Ancient Comedy
description: A study of ancient Greek and Roman comedy, including authors such as Aristophanes, Menander, Plautus, and Terence. Issues connected to performance, textual interpretation and the social role of comedy will be explored.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 307.

subject: CLAS
title: Hellenistic Literature and Society
description: The cultural legacy of Hellenistic Alexandria, with focus on scientific, mathematical, literary, philological, philosophical, and religious developments and innovations.

prerequisites.text: HIST 205 or HIST 231 or permission of the instructor.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 305.

subject: CLAS
title: The Greek and Roman Novel
description: A study of the ancient novel, including Petronius, The Satyricon, Apuleius, The Golden Ass and Longus, Daphnis and Chloe. Issues connected to the novel's development and generic formations, its social and historical contexts, and influence will be discussed.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 309.

subject: CLAS
title: Classical Tradition
description: Examines the evolution of Classical Antiquity's social and cultural status from the 17th c. to the present day. Particular consideration is given to the processes of the ongoing professionalization of history and archeology as academic disciplines, the emergence of new political usages of the past, the transformation of cultural practices from the Grand Tour to the modern museum and tourism.

prerequisites.text: CLAS 202 or related courses or permission of instructor

subject: CLAS
title: The Epic Tradition
description: The course covers major epics of the Mediterranean world such as the Epic of Gilgamesh, Homer's Iliad and Odyssey, Apollonius' Argonautica, Vergil's Aeneid, Ovid's Metamorphoses, Lucan's Bellum Civile, and Statius' Thebaid. Issues connected to social and cultural context, performance, literary theory, and interpretation will be discussed.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 371.

notes: Texts taught in translation, no knowledge of ancient Greek or Latin required.

subject: CLAS
title: Greek and Roman Historiography
description: Seminar on the works of the Greek and Roman historians (in translation) who founded a new literary genre for the exploration of past and present events; interpretation of their approaches towards history and theories for their study.

prerequisites.text: 3 credits in Classics at the 300 level or up or permission of instructor.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 490.

subject: CLAS
title: Ancient Lyric and Elegy
description: This course examines the Lyric and Elegiac genres from Greece (700 BCE) to Imperial Rome (100 CE). Authors such as Archilochus, Sappho, Alcaeus, Callimachus, Catullus, Propertius and Ovid will be situated in their social and historical contexts as the class addresses issues of poetics, politics, sexuality, and culture.

subject: CLAS
title: Greek and Roman Oratory
description: Greek and Roman Oratory situates the works of authors such as Plato, Demosthenes, Aeschines, Cicero and Tacitus in their social and historical contexts, in addition to examining ancient oratorical theory, education, political science, and culture.

subject: CLAS
title: Ancient Didactic Poetry
description: Ancient Didactic Poetry examines the works of authors such as Hesiod, Empedocles, Aratus, Lucretius, Vergil, Ovid and Manilius. The works are set in their original historical and social contexts while issues related to intellectual history, ancient cosmology, poetry and culture are considered.

subject: CLAS
title: Advanced Latin: Authors
description: Translation and discussion of selections from ancient Latin literature written by a single author or several authors closely linked by genre or historical period. Emphasis on developing reading proficiency. Texts change from year to year. Course may be taken more than once.

prerequisites.text: CLAS 312 or permission of instructor

notes: This is a language course. Reading knowledge of Latin is expected.

subject: CLAS
title: Advanced Latin: Themes
description: Examination of a theme or problem in Roman literature, culture or history through the translation and discussion of ancient Latin texts. Emphasis on close reading and analysis of ancient Latin. Texts change from year to year. Course may be taken more than once.

prerequisites.text: CLAS 312 or permission of instructor

notes: This is a language course. Reading knowledge of Latin is expected.

subject: CLAS
title: Advanced Ancient Greek: Authors
description: Translation and discussion of selections from ancient Greek literature written by a single author or several authors closely linked by genre or historical period. Emphasis on developing reading proficiency. Texts change from year to year. Course may be taken more than once.

prerequisites.text: CLAS 322 or permission of instructor

subject: CLAS
title: Advanced Ancient Greek: Themes
description: Examination of a theme or problem in ancient Greek literature, culture or history through the translation and discussion of ancient Greek texts. Emphasis on close reading and analysis of ancient Greek. Texts change from year to year. Course may be taken more than once.

prerequisites.text: CLAS 322 or permission of instructor

notes: This is a language course. Reading knowledge of Ancient Greek is expected.

subject: CLAS
title: Medieval Greek
description: Readings by Greek authors writing during the Late Imperial through Byzantine periods

prerequisites.text: CLAS 312 or permission of instructor

subject: CLAS
title: Advanced Topics
description: An in-depth look at various topics in classical studies.

prerequisites.text: Any ancient history course or 300-level Classics course or permission of instructor.

subject: CLAS
title: Greco-Roman Religious Literature
description: Examination of works of Greek and Roman literature that either deal extensively with theology and religion as themes or were implicated directly in religious practice. Authors or texts such as Hesiod, the Homeric Hymns, Plato, the Derveni Papyrus, Varro, Cicero, Philo and Augustine will be considered.

subject: CLAS
title: Independent Research
description: Under the direction of an instructor, an independent research course that makes use of ancient texts in their original language.

prerequisites.text: Written permission of instructor. Student must have extensive background in the proposed area of study.

notes: Permission must be obtained from the department before registration.

subject: CLAS
title: Internship: Classics
description: Internship with an approved host institution or organization.

prerequisites.text: Permission of the departmental Internship Adviser.

restrictions.text: Open to U2 and U3 students with a minimum CGPA of 2.7, and permission of the departmental Internship Advisor

notes: Course may only be taken once

A student may not count both CLAS 498 and CLAS 499 towards the Minor, Major or Joint Honours programs in Classics. Both CLAS 498 and 499 may be counted towards the Honours program in Classics only with permission of the program advisor

subject: CLAS
title: Classics Seminar
description: Seminar on a topic in ancient Greek or Roman literature and society. Topic varies by year.

restrictions.text: Open to U2 or U3 Honours students and MA students or by permission of instructor

subject: CLAS
title: Methods in Latin Literature in Translation
description: Survey of Latin Literature in translation, confronting questions of genre and situating texts in their social and historical contexts, including epic, lyric, didactic, bucolic, and elegiac poetry; comedy and tragedy, historiography, and rhetoric.
notes: May be taken only once for credit.

subject: CLAS
title: Methods in Ancient Greek Literature in Translation 1
description: Survey of Ancient Greek Literature in translation, confronting questions of genre and situating texts in their social and historical contexts, including epic, lyric and bucolic poetry; Classical tragedy, comedy, historiography, and rhetoric.
notes: May be taken only once for credit.

subject: CLAS
title: Research in Latin Literature in Translation
description: Readings, discussion, and research in Classical Latin literature on a specific topic or theme through translated texts.

prerequisites.text: CLAS 605 or permission of the instructor

notes: Topic changes from semester to semester.
Can be repeated for credit.

subject: CLAS
title: Research in Ancient Greek Literature in Translation
description: Readings, discussion, and research in Ancient Greek literature on a specific topic or theme through translated texts.

prerequisites.text: CLAS 606 or permission of the instructor

notes: Topic changes from semester to semester.
Can be repeated for credit.

subject: CLAS
title: Intensive Latin Review
description: Intensive review of advanced Latin grammar, morphology, syntax and vocabulary, and strategies and techniques for advanced translation prose and poetry.
notes: Designed for graduate students based on placement to be completed before enrolling in CLAS 610 or CLAS 612.

subject: CLAS
title: Readings in Latin Literature
description: Translation and analysis of selected texts in Latin. Authors or texts change from year to year. This course may be taken more than once.

subject: CLAS
title: Topics in Latin Literature
description: Examination of a selected topic in Latin literature through the translation and analysis of relevant Latin texts. Topics vary by year. Course may be taken more than once.

subject: CLAS
title: Intensive Ancient Greek Review
description: Intensive review of advanced grammar, morphology, syntax and vocabulary of ancient Greek, and strategie and techniques for advanced translation of prose and poetry.
notes: Designed for graduate students based on placement to be completed before enrolling in CLAS 620 or CLAS 622.

subject: CLAS
title: Readings in Ancient Greek Literature
description: Translation and analysis of selected texts in ancient Greek. Authors or texts change from year to year. This course may be taken more than once.

subject: CLAS
title: Topics in Ancient Greek Literature
description: Examination of a selected topic in ancient Greek literature through the translation and analysis of relevant ancient Greek texts. Topics vary by year. Course may be taken more than once.

subject: CLAS
title: Methods in Ancient Mediterranean Religion 1
description: Topics in ancient Greek and/or Roman religion. Introduction to the historiography of the field, its central questions, theoretical approaches, and methods.
notes: Topic changes from year to year.
May only be taken once for credit.

subject: CLAS
title: Methods in Ancient Mediterranean Religion 2
description: Studies in ancient Mediterranean religions. Thematic focus includes ritual and practice, ritual and practice, the concept of the divine and pantheons, the afterlife, the intersection of religion and philosophy, the role of religion in empire, the emergence of Christianity, and its development. Focus on ancient Greek and/or Roman contexts.
notes: Topic changes year by year.
May be repeated for credit.

subject: CLAS
title: Research in Ancient Mediterranean Religions
description: Readings, discussion, and research on a topic in ancient Greek or Roman religion

prerequisites.text: CLAS 631, CLAS 632, or permission of the instructor

notes: Topic changes year by year.
May be repeated for credit.

subject: CLAS
title: Methods in Classical Archaeology 1
description: Investigation of the historiography, theoretical approaches, and methods employed in the field of classical archaeology. Focus on the Greek and/or Roman Mediterranean, broadly construed.
notes: Themes and topics might change from year to year.
May only be taken once for credit

subject: CLAS
title: Methods in Classical Archaeology 2
description: Case studies in classical archaeology from the Greek and Roman Mediterranean. Focus on specific sites, objects, and artworks to elaborate broader theoretical and methodological issues in the field.
notes: Topics might vary year to year.
May only be taken once for credit.

subject: CLAS
title: Research in Classical Archaeology
description: Readings, discussion, and research on a topic in classical archaeology.

prerequisites.text: CLAS 646, CLAS 647, or permission of the instructor

notes: Topic changes year-to-year.
May be repeated for credit.

subject: CLAS
title: Archeological Fieldwork in Italy
description: Archaeological fieldwork in Italy; emphasis on archaeological field methods, laboratory work, and theoretical interpretation of archaeological data in an Italian archaeological context. Taught at an archaeological site in Italy.

prerequisites.text: Permission of instructor

notes: Students are responsible for their own airfare to Italy.

There is a fee of $2850.44 for the McGill Salapia Field School in Italy associated with registration in CLAS 649. The fee includes shared apartment accommodation for groups of four students, meals (breakfast, lunch and dinner M-R and breakfast and lunch M-F), field tools and weekday transportation to and from the dig site. Students are responsible for their own travel arrangements to Puglia and travel insurance costs.

subject: CLAS
title: Seminar
description: Topics in ancient Greek or Roman literature, culture, and society. Emphasis on the reading and interpretaton of texts in ancient Greek and Latin.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 691.

subject: CLAS
title: Methods in Classical Reception 1
description: Investigation of the historiography of classical reception as a field, and the theories and methods employed in its study.
notes: Topic varies year-by-year.
May only be taken once for credit.

subject: CLAS
title: Methods in Classical Reception 2
description: A study of classical reception through case studies that underscore the diversity of media and message through time, and the significance of these patterns of engagement.
notes: Topics and texts/media change year-by-year.
May only be taken once for credit.

subject: CLAS
title: Research in Classical Reception
description: Readings, discussion, and research on a topic in classical reception.

prerequisites.text: CLAS 653, CLAS 654, or permission of the instructor

notes: Topic changes year-by-year
May be repeated for credit.

subject: CLAS
title: Modern Greek 1
description: Intensive reading of Modern Greek poetry in the original language.

subject: CLAS
title: Modern Greek 2
description: Intensive reading of Modern Greek prose in the original language.

prerequisites.text: CLAS 678

subject: CLAS
title: M.A.Research Project 1
description: Start of the production of a research project under the supervision of a faculty member.

subject: CLAS
title: M.A.Research Project 2
description: Continued work on production of a research project under the supervision of a faculty member.

subject: CLAS
title: M.A.Research Project 3
description: Completion of a research project under the supervision of a faculty member.

subject: CLAS
title: Methods Seminar
description: Selected topics in the diverse research methods deployed in classical studies, including (but not limited to) different approaches to interpreting ancient evidence, the acquisition of research skills, grant writing, and publication strategies.

subject: CLAS
title: M.A. Thesis Proposal
description: Preparatory work for the writing of an M.A. thesis under the supervision of the thesis advisor(s), leading to a thesis proposal.

subject: CLAS
title: M.A. Thesis Research 1
description: Continued work for the writing of an M.A. thesis under the supervision of the thesis advisor(s), including production of an annotated bibliography.

subject: CLAS
title: M.A. Thesis Research 2
description: Continued work under the supervision of the thesis advisor(s).

subject: CLAS
title: M.A. Thesis Submission
description: Continued work under the supervision of the thesis advisor(s), leading to completion and submission.

subject: CLAS
title: Tutorial
description: Individualized guided research on an approved topic.
